title: 〜ばかりか / 〜ばかりでなく
meaning: not only… but also… (something even greater)
simpleExplanation: 〜ばかりか means "not only X, but also Y", where Y is more surprising or more serious than X. It piles up facts in the same direction: both good things, or both bad things. 〜ばかりでなく is the same idea in a slightly plainer, more neutral tone.
whenUsed: ばかりか is mainly written or formal spoken; ばかりでなく is used in both speech and writing. だけでなく is the everyday equivalent. Typical situations: praising someone's many skills, describing an escalating problem, or listing effects of a change.
formation: Verb (plain form) + ばかりか / ばかりでなく
な-adjective + な / である + ばかりか
Noun + ばかりか / ばかりでなく

parts.role: predicate shared by X and Y

diagram.translation: He can speak not only English but also Chinese and Russian.

examples.ja: 彼は英語ばかりか、中国語やロシア語も話せる。
examples.reading: かれはえいごばかりか、ちゅうごくごやロシアごもはなせる。
examples.en: He can speak not only English but also Chinese and Russian.

examples.ja: この地域は交通が不便なばかりか、店も少ない。
examples.reading: このちいきはこうつうがふべんなばかりか、みせもすくない。
examples.en: Not only is transport inconvenient in this area, there are few shops too.
examples.note: な-adjective + な + ばかりか.

examples.ja: 彼は約束を守らなかったばかりか、謝りもしなかった。
examples.reading: かれはやくそくをまもらなかったばかりか、あやまりもしなかった。
examples.en: Not only did he break his promise, he didn't even apologize.

examples.ja: この薬は効果がないばかりでなく、副作用もある。
examples.reading: このくすりはこうかがないばかりでなく、ふくさようもある。
examples.en: This medicine is not only ineffective, it also has side effects.

examples.ja: 彼女は仕事ができるばかりでなく、人柄もいい。
examples.reading: かのじょはしごとができるばかりでなく、ひとがらもいい。
examples.en: She is not only good at her job but also has a lovely personality.

similarGrammar.difference: Everyday equivalent, neutral. ばかりか sounds more written and emphasizes the surprising second item.
Formal, written "not only". Even stiffer than ばかりか.
Reverses the first item ("far from X"). ばかりか keeps X true and adds Y.
"X goes without saying, and also Y": X is obvious, Y is added.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は英語ばかりか、日本語は話せない。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は英語ばかりか、日本語も話せる。／彼は英語どころか、日本語も話せない。
commonMistakes.why: ばかりか needs both clauses pointing the same way. To deny both, use どころか.

commonMistakes.wrong: 親切ばかりか、頭もいい。
commonMistakes.right: 親切なばかりか、頭もいい。
commonMistakes.why: 親切 is a な-adjective and needs な before ばかりか.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は歌がうまいばかりか、踊ってください。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は歌がうまいばかりか、ダンスも上手だ。
commonMistakes.why: The second clause must be a statement, not a request or command.

usageNotes: The second clause almost always has も, さえ, or まで to mark the added item.
ばかりか is often used for negative escalation (broke a promise + didn't apologize); ばかりでなく is more neutral.
In casual speech, だけじゃなくて replaces both.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, if the second clause adds a bigger item of the same kind (〜も / 〜まで), choose ばかりか. If it reverses the first, choose どころか.
Distractors: どころか, ばかりに, ばかりだ, ばかりで. Only ばかりか / ばかりでなく mean "not only".
In 並べ替え, place X + ばかりか first and the も-phrase after it.
